nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Three days of nothing. Then on the Wednesday, one letter, from a woman two hours up the coast.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: She'd heard the ask. Did Margo say anything, to anyone. She wrote back: once. To me.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: There was a screenshot attached. I read it twice before I did anything else.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The coast road runs north out of Havenbay for two hours, and there isn't much on it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Margo Rivera drove it every second Sunday for eleven years, to a person none of the other three ever heard named.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I drove it on a Thursday. I kept thinking how ordinary it must have got for her.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Her name is Tessa. She was Margo's partner for eleven years. Nobody in Havenbay knew she existed.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Margo had a whole second room to her life, and she kept the door shut. Tessa says it never looked like effort.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: There was a card in Margo's kitchen drawer. In case, ring Tessa, and a number. She wrote it eleven years ago.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: After the harbour, the police found the card and rang the number. That's how Tessa learned Margo was dead. From a stranger, reading it out.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Tessa's frightened of being found. Eleven years of keeping quiet taught her something, and she said it plainly: a sentence can be an address.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: She said yes anyway. I drove home slower than I drove up.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The screenshot is real. I had it checked, and the date on it holds. Seventy-seven days after Violet died, about two and a half weeks after Brad drove to Kestrel Head.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: It's a message from Margo to Tessa, on the app they used. It says: The thing in the cupboard is wrong. It can't mean that.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Tessa kept it because Margo didn't say things like that. She asked what cupboard. Margo never answered, and never brought it up again.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The cupboard is what the four of them called Violet's locker. Margo doubted what was in it. She said so once, to one person, and then she stopped.

decision.prompt: So do I put Margo's own words on air, or keep them back and say it my way?

options.label: Air her words, no name, no town
options.result: The exact words go out. Exact words sometimes draw exact answers. And Tessa's fear goes out with them, whether I name her or not.

options.label: Paraphrase, and keep Tessa out of it
options.result: I'll say what Margo meant, not what she typed. No quotation, no app, no Sunday. Tessa's safer. The city hears less.

after.speaker: Ally Quinn
after.line: Either way, it's the only doubt Margo is known to have said out loud, and she said it to the one person none of them knew.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I've put the letter up on the board, line by line, next to what the room verified last month.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Liam's third of the yard, true. The boat requests, true. The lock changed and the key taken in, true. Every line the police could check, they checked, and it held.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: One line nobody checked. The kind one. Brad had paid the van money back that autumn. Nobody looked at it, because why would you look at a kind thing.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: And across all of it, Margo's sentence on a pin. The thing in the cupboard is wrong.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Here's where I've got to, and I'll say exactly this much. If the thing in the cupboard was wrong, then there was a thing, and something about it didn't fit.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I don't know what Margo meant. I'm not saying the letter's false. I'm not saying who.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: But there's a plainer question. What did Violet have in her last months that she hadn't had before?

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The gilded panel. She carried it round the trade, workshop to workshop, showing people. Nobody has seen it since.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: It isn't in the locker. It isn't in Brad's boxes. It isn't in the estate. I've asked. Something is missing from the world, and I don't know if it's the same something.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: One more word, and then I'll leave it. That. It can't mean that.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Not it can't be true. Not it can't be hers. It can't mean that. Margo had a meaning in her head, and she was refusing it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I've written the question on a card and pinned it under her sentence. What couldn't it mean? Nobody alive can tell me. So it stays up.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Last week I asked whether Margo Rivera said anything, to anyone. Three days of nothing. Then one answer. One.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Here's what I can tell you. The letter in Violet's locker listed things that were wrong in her house. The police checked every line they could, and every line held.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: One line nobody checked, because it was kind. And one thing Violet had in her last months, a gilded panel she showed round the trade, that nobody has seen since. Not in the locker. Not anywhere I can find.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: I'm not telling you the letter's false. I'm not telling you who. I'm telling you something is missing from the world, and if you've seen it, write to me, not to anyone else.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: The four of them had a name for Violet's locker. The cupboard. And Margo Rivera, who everybody thought said nothing, said one thing about it.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Seventy-seven days after Violet died, she wrote to a woman two hours up the coast: The thing in the cupboard is wrong. It can't mean that. This is Echoes of Havenbay, I'm Ally Quinn. Goodnight for now, Harbour. Sleep tight.

nodes.speaker: Ally Quinn
nodes.line: Margo doubted what was in the cupboard. Not that it was Violet's. What it meant. She said so once, to one person, and never again. This is Echoes of Havenbay, I'm Ally Quinn. Goodnight for now, Harbour. Sleep tight.
